title: Your Emergency Fund: A Safety Net for Unexpected Events
summary: An emergency fund is money set aside for unexpected costs, like job loss or medical needs, to avoid debt.

sections.heading: Why You Need an Emergency Fund
sections.body: Life in India can bring unexpected events. Job loss is common as there are no general unemployment benefits. Family support is important, but your own savings provide a crucial safety net. An emergency fund helps you cover costs without borrowing at high rates like 42% from credit cards or 60% from informal lenders.

sections.heading: How Much to Save
sections.body: Aim to save enough to cover 3 to 6 months of your essential living expenses. This fund should be easily accessible, like in a bank savings account, which offers instant access and no risk. While it earns low interest (around 2.7%), its main purpose is safety, not high returns.

sections.heading: Where to Keep Your Emergency Fund
sections.body: A regular bank savings account is ideal for instant access and zero risk. For slightly better returns (around 6.5%) with easy access, consider a Recurring Deposit or Fixed Deposit, protected up to ₹5 lakh by DICGC. Avoid locking money in long-term products like PPF or investments like Nifty 50 index funds for your emergency fund.

example.title: Rohan's Rainy Day Savings
example.body: Rohan, who just started his first job, earns ₹30,000 per month. He decides to build an emergency fund. He calculates his essential monthly expenses at ₹15,000 and aims for 3 months of coverage, meaning ₹45,000. He sets up a recurring deposit (RD) at his bank, depositing ₹5,000 each month. After 9 months, he will have his ₹45,000 emergency fund ready, earning about 6.5% interest.

takeaway: An emergency fund is your first financial priority, providing security against job loss, medical issues, or other unforeseen expenses.
